project_metadata.objective: Predict mental health scores from lifestyle and behavioral factors

dataset_info.data_source: Kaggle - Tech Use and Stress Wellness Dataset
dataset_info.note: Landing page '125,000+ data points' = 5,000 participants × 25 features

model_performance.r_squared_interpretation: Model explains 85.6% of variance in mental health scores
model_performance.rmse_interpretation: Average prediction error of ±5.07 points on mental health scale
model_performance.model_fit_quality: Excellent (R² > 0.70 is considered strong in social science)
model_performance.remaining_variance: 14.4% likely due to unmeasured factors (social support, genetics, life events)

stress_level.interpretation: Each 1-point stress increase → -3.0 point mental health decline

physical_activity.example: Increasing from 2 to 5 hours/week = ~4.5 point improvement

sleep_quality.interpretation: Each 1-point sleep quality gain → +1.8 point improvement

health_behavior_score.interpretation: Composite metric with minor negative effect
health_behavior_score.note: Unexpected negative coefficient likely due to multicollinearity with component features

sleep_duration.interpretation: Each additional hour of sleep → +0.2 point improvement

mindfulness_minutes.interpretation: Each additional daily minute → +0.02 point improvement

caffeine_intake.interpretation: Minimal effect (100 mg caffeine → -0.2 point change)

stress_management_priority.finding: Stress has 3x more impact than any positive factor
stress_management_priority.business_implication: Stress reduction features should be top priority

physical_activity_roi.finding: Each hour of weekly activity = +1.5 mental health points
physical_activity_roi.business_implication: Activity tracking features have high ROI

sleep_quality_vs_duration.business_implication: Prioritize sleep quality tools over sleep duration tracking

mindfulness_caffeine_minimal.finding: Mindfulness (+0.022) and caffeine (-0.002) have minimal direct effects
mindfulness_caffeine_minimal.interpretation: These factors may work indirectly through stress/sleep
mindfulness_caffeine_minimal.business_implication: Don't over-invest in caffeine tracking features

assumptions: Linear relationships between predictors and mental health
limitations: Self-reported data subject to recall and social desirability bias
Synthetic/survey data may not represent real device telemetry
Missing socioeconomic, ethnicity, and clinical diagnosis variables
Model trained on available features; unmeasured factors explain 14.4% variance
model_assumptions_and_limitations.interpretation_caveat: All findings represent correlations, not causation

engineered_features_created: health_behavior_score (composite of mindfulness, healthy eating, wellness app use)
feature_engineering_summary.purpose: Transform raw behavioral data into interpretable lifestyle metrics

data_validation.outliers_handled: Yes (outliers in screen time and activity hours capped)
data_validation.train_test_split: Not documented (full dataset used for regression)
